intro: Tuvalu is one of the world's smallest countries, nine low coral islands threatened by rising seas.

chapters.title: Polynesian settlers
text: Polynesian voyagers from Samoa and Tonga settled the islands about 2,000 years ago. 'Tuvalu' means 'eight standing together', for the eight inhabited islands at independence.

chapters.title: Ellice Islands
text: Britain ruled the islands, then called the Ellice Islands, together with the Gilbert Islands (now Kiribati). In 1974 the Ellice Islanders voted to separate.

chapters.title: Independence and climate
text: Tuvalu became independent in 1978. In 2023 it signed a treaty with Australia letting up to 280 Tuvaluans a year move there, because of the threat from rising seas.

keyTerms.meaning: Oceans rising as the climate warms.
